title: Entering a group dims the layer list but not the canvas
detail: SPLIT, and the two halves went opposite ways. The canvas half STAYS OPEN as a decision, not a bug: the dim was declined because opacity is in Fabric stateProperties, so dimming the canvas would serialise view state into every save, which §67 forbids. That reasoning still holds and nothing here overturns it. The layer half was not a decision at all but a defect, and it was worse than this row says — the row recorded that the list dims today (data-context=false), which is true only after something unrelated re-projects the tree. Fixed as vg-058.

title: The line chart occasionally slides left as if correcting a position
detail: NOT REPRODUCED in 30 seconds of live playback against a real host, and BOTH of the rows named candidates are ruled out for that window. The row guessed a resize observer re-fitting mid-animation, or a chart settling after a viewport change; neither fired: the viewport transform was byte-identical at the start and the end (0.61602870 with the same offset, zero changes in thirty samples), the chart own box never moved (left 616, top 695, 963x215, angle 0, scale 1 and 1), and a ResizeObserver on the body fired once, which is the probe own DOM reads rather than anything the chart did. STILL OPEN, because occasionally is rarer than thirty seconds and closing it on a non-reproduction would be the same mistake as filing it on a screenshot. WHAT THE NEXT ATTEMPT SHOULD USE, because two attempts here failed for one reason and the reason is worth keeping: counting ink in the chart region cannot see this. The card is opaque and the sampled rect includes the dark part of the backdrop, so every column reads as drawn and every column reads as dark — the first probe reported a constant firstX of 0 and lastX of the full width, and a luminance profile reported the same. Watching the EVENTS is what separates a slide from data changing, because data moves locally and a slide moves everything.

title: The preview data source fluctuates faster than a real PC
detail: "The Preview data source fluctuate too rapidly which is not realistic to a normal PC hardware behavior, and a bit distracting for the author." The cadence is a number in fake-source. 'Realistic' needs a decision about what the preview is for.

title: The top bar becomes a toolbar of icon buttons on the theme document, and its commands are renamed
detail: "The top bar menu is kinda lost in direction of what's it for. Some are legitimate functions you can't find anywhere else (File & View menus), but Edit & Insert is a duplication of actions that already in their rightful places. Verdict: Make it an actual toolbar (icon buttons, not nested inside a menu) with actions to the theme document, not individual elements." AND the rename, in full: Save Package -> Activate (instructs the player to switch to this theme); Release Package -> Export theme; Open Package -> Import theme; Open library -> Open; Save to library -> Save; ADD a Save as button; New from starter -> New from template (only one template today, more are coming). Note Activate and Save as are missing capabilities, not renames: the host already stores the active theme and the theme route is a PUT to a named id, so each is one id away. Do this as one change, not seven renamings — the Arrange menu was already removed on exactly this reasoning (vg-016), and doing the buttons without the toolbar shape means doing the work twice.

title: Should the editor be rebuilt on Base UI + shadcn/ui + Tailwind before further micro-adjustments?
detail: "Honestly the entire editor UI is kind of boring, primitive & unpolish... Should we do a whole redesign of it with Base UI - Shadcn - TailwindCSS, which has been in the queue long enough, before doing any micro adjustments to specific UI details? I'm talking about the whole panels rearrangement, too." The same question as vg-031 one level up, and the same wrong answer: the ecosystem search was run against Base UI alone. FIRST STEP IS NOT A REDESIGN — it is searching shadcn/ui for the panels this editor already has (dialog, select, tabs, popover, tooltip, slider, switch, scroll-area, separator) and finding out which replace hand-rolled equivalents. Then bring the result back to choose: full redesign first, or defect fixes first. Bigger than any other item here and deliberately unstarted. SEARCH RUN, AND THE PREMISE IS MOSTLY WRONG. The row asked for shadcn/ui to be searched for the nine panels the editor already has, and that search has now actually been run against shadcn rather than Base UI alone — the omission this row records as the reason it was answered wrong twice. RESULT ACROSS THE NINE: one is genuinely hand-rolled, seven are already better served by what the editor uses, and two do not exist at all. tooltip is the only real hand-roll (editor-shell/controls/tooltip.ts:54-145, 91 lines of placement and listener body). switch does not exist — the two cases are native checkboxes (glass.ts:205, chart-manager/panel.ts:215). separator does not exist either: no hr and no role=separator anywhere in src/web. tabs is already Base UI (shell-layout.tsx:2). popover is already a vendored shadcn component (components/ui/popover.tsx). dialog is native <dialog> with showModal at five sites, which shadcn would replace with a portal and lose the free focus trap, Escape, inert and top layer. select is native at TWENTY-THREE sites. slider is a native input type=range. scroll-area is native overflow carrying a deliberate scrollbar-gutter:stable. Verdict: zero adopt, one unclear, seven leave. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: every select, dialog, slider and checkbox lives in an IMPERATIVE .ts panel mounted into a React-owned host div, and the editor has exactly ten .tsx files, none of them panels. shadcn components are React function components, so "adopt shadcn Select" is not a component swap — it is Reactifying the panel layer, which IS the redesign. The row cannot be settled one component at a time, which is why it kept coming back. WHERE THE USERS ACTUAL COMPLAINT LIVES, which is not these nine: "boring, primitive & unpolish" plus panels rearrangement is a CSS and layout problem. The shell carries 841 lines across 131 hand-written editor-shell-* selectors with Tailwind INSTALLED AND UNUSED — zero Tailwind utility classes in the .tsx files, only the colour picker using it. If a redesign happens its subject is CSS consolidation and panel layout, not component adoption. ANSWER TO THE ROWS OWN QUESTION: defects first. TOLD AND NOT SETTLED BY ME: the Base-versus-Radix base is the users call, because switching components.json to the Base UI base would let the vendored popover drop Radix and make the next eight additions free of a second library — but it SUPERSEDES the vg-031 ruling that this field's ecosystem is shadcn-with-Radix, and the repo precedent (0020) is to ask rather than re-decide. A full Base UI variant of all nine does exist, so the second-headless-library objection does not apply at that base. COULD NOT ESTABLISH, and it matters to the verdict: no tsc run, so the typecheck reading rests on the one already-vendored example rather than a measurement; a raw-source fetch came back with generics and JSX stripped, so any "this does not typecheck" read of it would be a fetch artifact; and with no browser, nobody has said whether the running editor actually looks primitive — only that its chrome is hand-written CSS rather than a components library. OPERATIONAL NOTE: components.json EXISTS at src/web/packages/editor/components.json. The shadcn MCP resolves it from the workspace root, finds none, and reports no registries configured — passing registries: ["@shadcn"] explicitly makes every tool work. Nothing was created or configured to get there.

title: A desktop-shaped theme letterboxes to 31% of a phone's height
detail: MEASURED: the stress fixture at 412x839 gives an artboard of about 412x258 with bars above and below. Nothing overflows, nothing is cropped, no console errors — this is contain working exactly as §53 specifies. Filed because two rulings pull against each other and only the user can settle which wins: "a phone is the main display type" and "content is always contain" cannot both be satisfied by a desktop-shaped theme on a portrait phone, because the content will be whole and the text about 6px. Three ways out — leave it, add a per-display fit, or let a theme declare the size it is designed for — and which one is right depends on who reads these displays and from how far.

title: The line chart's Glass control: a Circle's frost reads stronger than a Rect's at the same value
detail: RULING STANDS: a slight per-shape difference is acceptable rather than no glass on closed shapes; the expensive option wins by default. CHARACTERISED, NOT FIXED, and the lead I gave the investigator was wrong. I offered "the Circle region measured 127,449 px against the Rect 156,009 for the same box" as proof the region was shape-dependent. It is not: that sweep gave every shape the same AUTHORING box, and a Circle has no 240x160. Both numbers reconstruct exactly at the sweep pad — 437x357 = 156,009 and 357x357 = 127,449, predicted ratio 0.8165 against 0.81691 measured. At one 260x260 box all five shapes take a byte-identical 362x362 region (131,044 px). PARTIAL COVERAGE REFUTED: no collapse at the rim, and the bin touching the boundary is the largest bin in three of four measurements. MATERIAL PARITY IS BIT-IDENTICAL: mean luma 94.75/94.75 over stripes and 93.41/93.41 over a photograph, distinct colours 40/40 and 10/10, and the frost boxes are pixel-identical at thresholds 2, 1.5 and 1. WHAT DIFFERS IS FOOTPRINT: a Circle covers 78.54% of its box, 21.5% less frosted area — which reads LIGHTER, not stronger, so it is the wrong direction to explain the report. STILL OPEN, and the leading hypothesis is not the renderer: a Circle authored size is a RADIUS and a Rect authored size is a WIDTH, so the same number gives a disc twice the area. Checked and not yet confirmed in the scene where it was seen. glass.ts is byte-identical to the base sha; nothing was simulated away, per the ruling. THE AUTHORS PATH TO THIS COMPARISON IS REACHABLE AFTER ALL, and I said otherwise earlier and was wrong twice about it. First: I claimed the Glass blur control does not exist on a chart. It does not exist on a chart because a chart cannot be frosted — the control appears once there is a radius to tune, and I compared an object that was refused against one that already had frost on. Second: I then said the report could not have come from the editor because the line charts control cannot be changed. True, and beside the point: the report is about a CIRCLE and a RECT, and both are perfectly authorable. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY SHAPE, which is also the ruling ADR-0015 predicts: Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon all offer an ENABLED Frosted glass control; Polyline and Line are aria-disabled, correctly, having no closed area to frost. And the two shapes the report names get the SAME DEFAULT: a fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both become vigiliaGlass at blurRadius 16 the moment frost is switched on, with the blur control appearing alongside it. So the situation the report describes — a Circle and a Rect at the same value — is exactly what the product produces by default, and the row stands on its own merits again. What remains is what the earlier characterisation established and this does not change: over the area they share the frost is bit-identical, and what differs is footprint, a Circle covering 78.54 percent of its box. If a Circle reads stronger, the leading hypothesis is still the authors own — a Circle size is a RADIUS where a Rectangle size is a WIDTH — and it is still unconfirmed in the scene where it was seen.
check: Measured across every shape in the running editor: Frosted glass is enabled on Rect, Circle, Ellipse, Triangle and Polygon, and aria-disabled on Polyline and Line with the reason on focus. A fresh Circle and a fresh Rectangle both take blurRadius 16 on the same click, and the Glass blur control appears only after that.

title: Auto-save, and a prompt for recovery after a browser crash
detail: RULED: draft in browser storage; write on a ~30 s timer and on leaving the page; recovery offers restore-or-discard naming what was lost; and the editor opens a theme from the library, which is the seam the other two need. BLOCKED: the asset-ownership question decides where the draft lives — if the editor stops holding asset bytes and the host owns them, the draft is a host write and browser storage is wrong.

title: What is derived state in a persisted Fabric object?
detail: The dirty guard's cause (vg-026) is one field of a general question, and patching styles alone leaves the next per-character cache to arrive and be found by the user. SCENE_PERSISTED_PROPERTIES is an allowlist that already intends to do this job and is not applied on the way out. The spec should answer which Fabric properties are derived from telemetry or from rendering, how a serialisation excludes all of them, and whether the allowlist should be enforced at the boundary. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-asset-ownership.md. AND NOW THERE IS A SHARP INSTANCE OF IT, MEASURED, which is vg-026. The dirty guard compares a document key against one captured when the editor was built, and with no input at all 13 of the Starter 52 objects change between 0.4 and 1.9 seconds after load — every one a Textbox, repainted by the live preview pass. The document differs from itself with nothing touched, so every New asks the author to save work nobody did. That is what the allowlist was meant to stop and does not reach: the changed objects are bound text, and what the live pass writes is the same property the author edits. This row is therefore not an abstract design question any more — it is one concrete false prompt an author meets on the first Ctrl+N, and the fix belongs here rather than in the dirty guard.

title: The artboard is not a clipping area, and neither repair is free
detail: Fabric has no scene-level clip: clipPath is per-object and serialised through cacheProperties, so it collides with the crop manager's authored per-image clip and with the derived text-box clip. Two candidate repairs, both with consequences — a scene Group wrapper changes what canvas.getObjects() means, which is the layer tree's and every walk over it. A decision, not a patch. Related: a selection handle should stay fully visible when its object is clipped (the user's own requirement in the same report).

title: Where the defect queue lives: the open-ended pass, the Superpowers lifecycle, and beads
detail: The working-out of whether every defect should become a spec and a plan (overkill), and where an open-ended queue sits beside a change lifecycle that has a finish line. Beads is proven installable natively on Windows (v1.3.0, no WSL) with the full lifecycle exercised; bd init edits AGENTS.md and installs hooks by default and --skip-agents declines that. Marked undecided by the user pending thought — specifically, not wanting two agent frameworks fighting each other. The registry is the incumbent until this is decided.

title: The layer list cannot select more than one row, and grouping needs a multi-selection
detail: The row click is onClick={() => selectLayer(row.id)} and ignores the event, so a shift-click on a second row replaces the first instead of adding to it. MEASURED: shift-clicking strapline after wordmark left only strapline selected, while the same two objects shift-clicked on the canvas select both. Grouping is reachable — the context menu offers Group once the selection is eligible — but only from a canvas multi-selection, so an author working in the layer list cannot make one. Needs a decision rather than a patch: whether a shift-click toggles a row the way the canvas does, whether shift extends a range like a file list, or whether the panel stays single-select and grouping moves somewhere reachable from it. An additive select also has to cross the Fabric-free bridge, which has one selectLayer(id) today.

title: Layer rows declare draggable but nothing consumes the drop, so reordering by drag does nothing
detail: MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because a row that does not reorder is only a finding if reordering is a thing the panel is offering. It is: every layer row carries draggable="true" in the DOM, which is an explicit promise that an HTML5 drag will be received and acted on. Nothing acts on it. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title changes the list not at all - the first eight rows are byte-identical before and after. That is true for a mouse drag and also for Playwright's dragTo, which is the technique that drives HTML5 drag-and-drop rather than mouse events, so this is not my probe using the wrong gesture. THE OPERATION ITSELF WORKS, which is what makes the dead attribute a real cost rather than an unimplemented feature: select the date text on the canvas, right-click, Bring to front, and the host's document moves date from index 6 to index 51 and every other object shifts down. So an author who wants to reorder can, by finding a context menu; an author who tries to drag, which is what the attribute invites and what every other layer panel in this class of tool invites, silently does nothing and gets no feedback. THE HONEST MITIGATING FACTOR: the row's cursor is default, not grab, so the panel does not visually advertise dragging - the promise is in the markup, not in the pixels. That is why this is filed as a smaller row than it first looks, and why the fix could legitimately be to drop the attribute rather than to implement the drop. What I would not accept is leaving an attribute that says draggable on an element where drag does nothing, because it is a false statement the next agent or the next tool will believe. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But the drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents, the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule. That is the row worth keeping, and it is filed as vg-099. vg-096 is CONFIRMED by the same measurement: cursor is auto on a draggable row. MEASURED LIVE ON A FRESH BUILD AND THE ROW IS WRONG AS FILED, in a way worth keeping. Dragging network-chart toward cpu-card-title does nothing, and it did nothing here too - both Playwright dragTo, which drives HTML5 drag-and-drop, and a raw mouse drag. But that drag was CROSS-PARENT and the panel refuses those by design: dragover marks only same-parent slots. Dragged between SIBLINGS the reorder works - network-down onto network-up swapped them, the list reading network-up,network-down before and network-down,network-up after. Every handler does run on the refused case: dragstart sets application/x-vigilia-layer, dragover is cancelled (defaultPrevented true), drop fires on the target row, and reorderLayer is reached. So the attribute is honest, the implementation is complete, and the row reported a deliberate restriction as a missing feature. THE REAL FINDING IS SMALLER AND MEASURED: the refusal is SILENT. Mid-gesture across parents the target row carries the same vigilia-layer-row class as before the drag began, the cursor stays auto, and no title or aria-description anywhere in the editor mentions group, parent, reorder or drag. An author who drags a row toward another group is given nothing at all - no indicator, no cursor, no rule - and cannot tell which case they are in until nothing happens. Filed as vg-099.

title: The type preset panel is not bound to the selection, so it contradicts the inspector it sits beside
detail: A DECISION, not a patch, and it is the real half of what vg-088 was filed as. Found while fixing vg-088. The type preset panel is constructed with (host, onChange, onDelete, fontActions) at editor-session.ts:320-337 — no canvas, no selection, no object reference — and its chooser defaults to Object.keys(presets)[0] at type-preset-manager/panel.ts:60-61. So it shows the first declared preset whatever the selection is set in. The vg-088 report established BOTH facts by probe, not inference: the inspector dropdown is correctly bound to typePresets.46-600, and the panel dropdown holds a bare 20-400 with CANVAS REFS: false. An author who sets a run to 24-400, opens the Type presets panel to see what that preset is, and finds 20-400 selected cannot tell a default from an answer. Note the shape: the two surfaces genuinely disagree, but not about a shared binding — one is bound and the other is unbound, so no fix to the binding reconciles them. Binding the panel to the selection changes what the panel IS (it is a document-level editor today), which is why it needs a decision rather than a patch.

title: Three owners of 'list the document's tokens by name' is the shape that let vg-093 exist
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-093 and vg-102, which is the third round of the same defect in this repo. artboard-panel.ts:519, palette-manager/panel.ts:214 and chart-manager/panel.ts:324 each build their own option list over the same globals, and each is a place a label can come out as an id instead of a name. vg-088 fixed runs.ts, vg-093 fixed the colour dropdown beside it, vg-102 fixed four resolution lines, and the next surface to print a raw ref will be one of these three. That is the point: the defect has been fixed three times in individual surfaces and the shape that permits it is untouched. ONE OWNER of 'list the document's references by name' is the fix, and it is a design call rather than a patch — the three lists differ in what they filter and what they do on an unresolvable token, so consolidating them means deciding what the shared function owes each caller. Worth noting what the fix already established: a token the author has DELETED is the one case where the raw ref is correct, because it is the only identifier left, and that case is pinned by a test.

title: Every chart repaint asks the whole canvas to redraw, and charts re-apply their options 30 times a second
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-081, which is where that fix's work stopped. Two costs, both on the idle path, both now the largest that remains. (1) scene-fabric/src/chart-object.ts:227 — every ECharts rendered event asks Fabric for a full-canvas render, measured at 525 of 624 canvas renders across 3 s of doing nothing at all. One chart's animation frame redraws the whole document. (2) ChartManager.refresh re-applies every chart's option at the chart refresh rate whether or not that chart's data moved; the rate is the author's own chartRefreshRate control, which is why this is a decision and not a patch — the View menu offers 30 FPS and 1 FPS and an author who picks either is choosing this cost. vg-081 removed the TEXT side of the same argument and the idle cost fell 14x; this is the other half. LEFT ALONE because chart-manager/ belonged to another agent during that pass and because (2) touches a control the user sets. Worth pairing with the decision the user already has open on vg-086's menu, since that is where the rate is chosen.

title: A text object's Height field reports what it was told, not what is drawn
detail: FOUND WHILE CLOSING vg-098, and recorded because it has already cost one measurement this pass. With a text object carrying no authored box — which is what the editor inserts — the Size H field reported 220 while the drawn box stayed about 70. The field echoes the number it was given rather than reading what the object measures, so it is not a reliable probe for a box write. That mattered concretely: an agent verifying the vertical alignment control read the Size field and the canvas, the two disagreed, and the field was the one that was wrong — twice, because the control itself turned out to be dead. Two findings had to be told apart before either could be fixed, and a third party reading the same field would draw the same wrong conclusion. Worth noting it is adjacent to vg-057, which seeded both dimensions of the box from the object's own measured edge so a first Size edit produces a whole box; this is the read side of the same seam, and it is pre-existing rather than introduced here. THE ROW DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and the disagreement was the instrument rather than the field. On every text object reachable through the editor's own controls the field and the object's own edge agree - measured cpu-card-title 27 against 27.12, a freshly inserted caption 79 against 78.83 - and readField re-reads the object on every render rather than echoing anything. Fabric's getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), and getCoords() reads a cache that assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight never invalidate, because they assign width and height directly rather than going through set (a set re-enters initDimensions). One object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). The 220-against-70 came from that. THE FIELD MUST KEEP SHOWING THE AUTHORED BOX - write puts the number the author types into vigiliaText.box, so a Size field reading the measured edge would name a number it is about to overwrite - but the box is stored UNSCALED, so a scaled text object draws a larger box and nothing said so. The field now says which is which where they differ: Size is the box the text was authored in (140 x 27). The object measures 280 x 54. STAYS OPEN because withdrawing is the user's call, alongside vg-087 which is also measured false. What is NOT uncertain is the real artefact underneath, filed as vg-112: the stale coordinate cache is not confined to a probe.

title: A theme that fails validation is answered 404, vanishes from the library, and the editor reports success
detail: MEASURED AT THE BOUNDARY while fixing vg-095, and the most serious thing either of those agents found. A theme sitting on disk whose metadata carries a stale locale key, or a stray backgroundMedia.scale, is answered 404 Theme not found, does not appear in the library listing, and the editor's boot-theme.ts openQuietly then opens a DIFFERENT theme and reports success naming that one. The validation issues are discarded at host/src/themes/store.ts:452-460. So there are three distinct outcomes collapsed into one silent one: the theme does not exist, the theme exists and is invalid, and the theme loaded - all of them read to an author as 'Theme not found' or as a success message about the wrong theme. The editor is the worse half, because it is the only one that says something untrue rather than nothing. AGENTS.md asks a 404 to name the cause it can prove (ADR-0018), and this one cannot prove it because the issues were thrown away before the response was built - which is precisely the fix: keep them, and answer a refused theme with what refused it. An author who hand-edited a theme, or who has a theme from a build whose schema has since tightened, currently has no way to learn any of that.

title: Sixteen of the envelope's shapes have no published counterpart, so a key added there is invisible to the schema
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-095. The decision note settles that the code owns the key list and the published schema is a hand-written contract held to it by a test - and that arrangement only covers what the schema publishes. Of the 23 shapes KNOWN_KEYS decides, only 7 appear in the schema at all. The other 16, including transform, node, textContent and the four chart settings shapes, live inside Fabric JSON that the schema validates as an opaque jsonValue, and fabric-envelope-schema-sync.test.ts forbids publishing the node tree. So a key added to one of those sixteen is invisible to anything validating against the published schema, which is the whole reason the two registries could disagree in the first place. The sync test catches disagreement where both sides speak; it is silent where only one does. Worth deciding whether that ceiling is accepted - a partially-describing published contract is a reasonable thing to publish, provided nobody reads it as total - or whether the sixteen need some other check. Also noted alongside: serialize.ts KEY_ORDER is a THIRD hand-written list of the same key names. It decides write order rather than membership, so it is not a second owner, but it moves with every key and nothing would notice if it stopped agreeing. AND THE GATE DID NOT CATCH IT WHEN IT HAPPENED, which is worth a line of its own. This row was briefly filed as "vg-vg-1101" — an id built by string-concatenating a formatted id — and backlog-check reported 21 items, all valid, without complaint. So the id check accepts a string that is not an id. That is a small hole in the gate every row depends on, since an id is what closes, what an artefact points at and what a commit trailer names, and it is filed by hand from a script often enough that the mistake is easy to make again.

title: Fabric's coordinate cache goes stale after the authored box is restored, so the selection frame, snapping and arrange work off the pre-pass size
detail: FOUND WHILE REFUTING vg-109, and it is the real artefact under that row's wrong measurement. assertBoxWidth and assertBoxHeight in scene-fabric/src/authored-box.ts:130,150 assign width and height DIRECTLY rather than through set, because a set re-enters initDimensions and would widen the object again - that is why they bypass it. But Fabric's aCoords is a separate cache, and bypassing set leaves it describing the PREVIOUS size. getBoundingRect() is makeBoundingBoxFromPoints(this.getCoords()), so everything that reads an object's box through the canvas reads a stale one: the SELECTION FRAME an author drags by, the SNAP positions the guides are computed against, and ARRANGE, which aligns selected objects to each other's edges. Measured: one text object read 172.78 x 102.7 stale, and 141 x 28.12 after a single dirty = true; setCoords(). A direct assignment or a setCoords after the restore would both be guesses until established, so the fix is to find where the pass leaves the object and mark it dirty once there - not to sprinkle setCoords at every reader. Left alone by the agent that found it because scene-fabric/ was held by another agent at the time, which is the disjoint-ownership rule working rather than a gap in it. This is worth its own row and its own dispatch: vg-089 already made a textbox's height a cache of its box, and this is the cost of that arrangement showing up somewhere the previous work did not measure.

title: The unit display options are four hardcoded English strings while every other list in the editor is Intl-derived
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-108, which swept the inspector's controls for association and turned up a different kind of problem on one of them. selection-inspector/runs.ts:648 builds the Unit display options from the literals "Default", "None", "Short" and "Long", where every other list the editor offers - palette tokens, type presets, the fifteen languages, the display zones - takes its labels from Intl.DisplayNames or a curated table. So a theme authored in another language meets four English words in the middle of an otherwise translated inspector. Small, and the same shape as the language row this pass withdrew: the fix is to ask Intl for these rather than to write them, and memory records that the instinct to probe Intl before hand-authoring a table is the right one here.

title: Two panels still carry controls with no id, because the assertion does not mount them
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING vg-108, whose generalised assertion is the point of that row and also its limit. The audit mounts the selection inspector in two disjoint field sets and three other panels, and it found twelve controls needing an id - all fixed. But asset-manager/panel.ts's two asset file inputs and new-document-chooser.ts's one select carry no id and were never mounted, so the assertion does not see them. Worth a row rather than a line because it is the failure mode of every generalised test: it covers what its author thought to mount, and a panel added later is invisible to it. The honest fix is either to mount these two or to state which panels the assertion covers so the next person adding one knows they are opting out. Recorded as open rather than closed because "the test passes" and "every control has an id" are different claims and only the first is currently true.

title: The reuse gate watchlists the repo-root scripts/ as a prefix, so a script directory under src/web/ is never gated
detail: FOUND WHILE LANDING THE FONT CATALOGUE GENERATOR, whose task brief instructed me to write a decision note first because scripts/ is on the gate watchlist and src/web/scripts/ is under it. Measured: it is not. reuse-gate.mjs:53 resolves every candidate path against the repo ROOT, so the watchlist entry scripts/ matches only a path whose repo-relative form begins scripts/ - and src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs does not. Piping that path into the gate returns 0 (allowed), while scripts/anything.mjs returns 2 (refused). So the second scripts/ directory in the repo is ungated and an agent can add a generator there without ever meeting the seven rungs. I landed the note anyway, because being told to is right and the gap is not mine to close silently, but the gate is not doing what its watchlist reads as saying. The fix is a judgement, not a typo: either add src/web/scripts/ as its own entry, or widen the matching so a bare directory name matches at any depth - which is the same shape as the bare-gitignore-pattern rule the repo already follows and would also catch a scripts/ under packages/. Worth deciding deliberately, because widening it means deciding what else under a path called scripts/ is a mechanism boundary.

title: Two of upstream registry titles disagree with the pairing document they point at, and one seeds the family the other names
detail: FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FONT CATALOGUE DEDUPE, and both instances are upstream bugs, not ours - we ship a workaround for the class and this row is the durable record of it. At Fonttrio commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403 the registry index contradicts its own pairing documents on two pairings out of 379, and in both cases the document is right. FIRST, the index is not one-to-one with its documents: it carries 380 entries for 379 distinct pairing names, because playfair-display-roboto is listed twice. Entry one is titled "Playfair Display Inter - Playfair Display + Inter + Inconsolata", entry two is titled "Playfair Display Roboto - Playfair Display + Roboto + Inconsolata", both carry the same url, and both resolve to one pairing document whose own title and cssVars name Roboto for the body role with an h1 weight of 800. So the index ships a title promising a family the record does not carry. SECOND, and independent of the duplicate: cormorant-garamond-proza-libre is titled "Cormorant Garamond Proza Libre" while its pairing document seeds Proza Libre for the heading, Cormorant Garamond for the body and JetBrains Mono for the mono - two family names run together with no separator and the mono family is absent from the title entirely. Its faces are correct, so the title is the whole defect there, where the first case is a duplicated record rather than a bad name. What made both findable is that nothing throws and the shape is valid: the catalogue is 379 unique ids of three faces each with correct weights and licences, so a count-based check passes. The test now asserts that a trio title ends with the three families it seeds, and it holds for 378 of 379 with this second case as the only exception - named in the test rather than waved through, so a third is red and a fix upstream is red too. Our workaround in docs/decisions/0024 is to treat the pairing document as the authority, keep the registry entry whose title matches it, require exactly one match and throw on none or two - so the duplicate resolves correctly today and a future contradiction stops the run instead of being guessed at. What is left for upstream is to drop the stale Inter entry or retitle it to the Roboto one the document serves, and to give cormorant-garamond-proza-libre a title that names its three families. Both are the same fix request and the same owner, which is why this is one row rather than two.
owner: upstream kapishdima/fonttrio registry.json at commit 8af7098ada0b90f076fbfe260244d11b05dd2403; workaround in src/web/scripts/generate-font-trios.mjs resolvePairings

title: The font catalogue spec says a facet keeps untagged entries, and the shipped query drops them
detail: FOUND IN TASK 4 REVIEW, on the spec's own wording, not on the code's. Two sentences in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md disagree with what ships: the Facets-are-derived paragraph (~:118-119) says "A pairing carrying no matching tag stays reachable by search: facets narrow the list, they never remove an entry from it", and the Verification > Browser paragraph (~:195) turns it into a gate, "a facet filters without hiding untagged entries". font-catalog-query.ts does the opposite and is right to: matchesFacet() returns values.includes(facet.value), so an untagged entry is dropped from the list. Strict filtering is the only reading under which "facets narrow the list" is true — keeping the union of tagged and untagged is the whole list, so the control would never filter anything. The operative guarantee the spec means is the narrower one, "stays reachable by search", and the code honours it in the one place it literally applies: queryFaces() keeps a face when ANY seeding trio carries the tag, since the face itself carries no tags. So the fix is a SPEC AMENDMENT, which is Task 8's line, and the browser gate has to move with it in the same edit or it asserts the opposite of the code and records a false pass. Task 6 should not be blocked on this: its picker ships strict filtering, which is correct either way.
owner: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-font-trio-catalog-design.md:118-119,195 (amendment and browser gate are Task 8's line)

title: The palette chip paints --shell-surface, which ember, moss and plum never declare, so three of the six chips are a coloured ring around editorial paper
detail: FOUND BY REVIEW of Task 1 (a pane bar replaces the rail) and not fixed there. .editor-shell-palette-swatch paints background: var(--shell-surface) with box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px var(--shell-accent), and it carries data-shell-palette={palette} so both tokens resolve against the palette it NAMES rather than the one in force. [data-shell-palette="ember"], "moss" and "plum" (editor-shell.css:53,57,61) declare only --shell-accent and --shell-warm, so --shell-surface falls through every ancestor to the :root editorial value #fffdf7: a saturated ring around an editorial-paper centre. Two owners could fix it and the choice is a design one - have those three palettes declare the surface their chip paints, or have the chip paint from tokens all six declare - so this is a row rather than a task. The plan does not own it: Task 2 fixes the --vigilia-* block and says the twelve --shell-* colour tokens are untouched, and its verification only covers elements styled from a --vigilia-* token.

title: The rebuild proof suite is red on the clean base: a button count, four inspector attributes and a run colour that no longer exist
detail: FOUND BY RUNNING author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts and author-journey-display.spec.ts during fix round 1 of the editor-left-column plan. Both are testIgnore d out of playwright.config.ts and run under playwright.rebuild.config.ts and playwright.display.config.ts, so npm run test:e2e never executes them and nothing else runs them either. Measured on 8adeb5c, the base before the pane bar landed: all 9 tests in the rebuild suite fail, and the display suite single test fails after 11.4m. Three causes, all predating that work. (1) author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts:76 asserts the Insert pane holds 13 buttons; 6fc9f27d halved SHAPE_KINDS to six on the user ruling recorded as vg-078, so it holds 11. (2) Nine references to [data-vigilia-panel-fill], -stroke, -border and -radius across author-journey-rebuild.spec.ts and rebuild-driver.ts: no such attribute exists anywhere in packages/editor/src, and 5a563a1c removed the last one on 2026-10-02. (3) [data-vigilia-run-colour=\"0\"] is asked for an option a blank theme does not carry, so the select resolves and the option never does. Not fixed at the time: not one of the nine can go green from a single line, and the suite has to be migrated onto the inspector attribute names that exist today, which is its own task with its own owner.
